readiness.summary: Deployz found a few things to address before this app can be deployed reliably.

findings.title: Tell Deployz how to start your app
findings.whyItMatters: Every deployment starts the app inside its container. Without a start command, the container exits immediately and the deployment never becomes healthy.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Add a CMD or ENTRYPOINT instruction to the Dockerfile (or a "start" script), or set the start command in the application details.
findings.technicalEvidence: The Dockerfile has no CMD or ENTRYPOINT instruction and no "start" script was found in any package.json.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: Deployz found container instructions but no command that starts the app.

findings.title: Give Deployz a way to update your database
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs your migration command automatically on every deploy, so each customer database always matches the code that talks to it.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Add a script that applies database migrations non-interactively (for example a "db:migrate" entry in package.json).
findings.technicalEvidence: A PostgreSQL library is present (pg (Ruby)) but no migration script was found in any package.json.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app uses a database, but Deployz could not find a command that updates the database structure during deploys.

findings.title: Background worker process
findings.whyItMatters: The worker starts with its own command, so background jobs keep running even when no web request comes in.
findings.suggestedOutcome: No change needed — Deployz will start the worker process alongside your app.
findings.technicalEvidence: Worker patterns detected: sidekiq, queue worker command, declared worker process (Procfile), declared worker process (docker-compose.production.yaml sidekiq)
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app declares a background worker process. Deployz runs it as a second container next to the web process.
